info.name: TradeLedger API
info.description:
Personal crypto trade journal and portfolio dashboard, synced automatically from the Bitunix exchange.

**Read-only against the exchange.** TradeLedger never places, modifies or cancels an order.

## Quick start

1. Select the **TradeLedger - Local** environment (or edit the collection variables).
2. Run **Auth > Login**. The token is saved to `{{token}}` automatically by a test script, and every other request inherits it from collection-level Bearer auth.
3. Run **Accounts > Create account** to get an `{{accountId}}`, then work through the other folders.

Requests that create something save the new id into a collection variable (`accountId`, `tradeId`, `planId`), so the folders can be run top to bottom, or with the Collection Runner.

## Static egress IP

Every Bitunix request is routed through a per-user proxy so the exchange always sees one static IP. Configure it under **Proxy** *before* attaching credentials. With `Proxy:Required` true (the default), a request with no proxy configured is refused rather than sent from the host address.

## How a trade reaches the journal

A closed Bitunix position becomes a journal row on its own. The mechanical half (prices, quantity, leverage, fees, funding, PnL) comes from the exchange; the subjective half (strategy, mental state, mistakes, rating) is supplied through `PATCH /api/trades/{id}/journal`.

All enums are sent and returned as strings, e.g. `"side": "Long"`, `"kind": "ExternalWallet"`.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Sign in and inspect the current user. Public signup is deliberately absent: the owner account is seeded at startup from configuration.

request.description:
Returns a bearer token for every other endpoint, and saves it to `{{token}}`.

Unknown email and wrong password give the same 401 on purpose, so the endpoint does not confirm which addresses exist.
The signed-in user plus their journal baseline: starting balance, journal start date, default risk per trade and display time zone. Everything is stored UTC; the time zone is for display only.

item.name: Proxy
item.description: The egress proxy every Bitunix request is routed through, so the exchange always sees one static IP. Set this before attaching API credentials: credential verification calls Bitunix and must originate from the allowlisted address.

request.description: Shows the proxy for the current user. The password is never returned, only `hasPassword`. `required` reflects Proxy:Required, and `configurationFallback` is the proxy from the Proxy section of configuration used when no per-user proxy is enabled.

Routes every Bitunix request for this user through a SOCKS5 proxy. The password is encrypted at rest with AES-GCM and never returned. Cached connections for the previous proxy are dropped immediately.

`scheme`: Http, Https, Socks5, Socks4, Socks4a.
Same thing over an HTTP CONNECT proxy. Omit username and password for an IP-allowlisted proxy that needs no authentication.
Clears the per-user proxy. With Proxy:Required true and no configuration fallback, every subsequent exchange request is refused rather than sent from the host address.

item.name: Accounts
item.description: Venues where value lives, and their encrypted exchange credentials.

request.description:
Every venue where value lives: Bitunix futures, Bitunix spot, external wallets and purely manual venues.

Credentials are never returned, only the last four characters of the API key so you can tell keys apart.

Registers a venue and saves the new id to `{{accountId}}`.

Bitunix futures and Bitunix spot are separate accounts. `trackedFrom` is the date the backfill stops walking back to.

`kind`: ExchangeFutures, ExchangeSpot, ExchangeWallet, ExternalWallet, ManualVenue.
`venue`: Bitunix, Manual. `syncMode`: Api, Manual.
A venue no API reaches. Holdings, transfers and balance snapshots for it are recorded by hand so the equity curve stays whole.

exec: // Names are unique per user, so keep re-runs from colliding (409).

request.description:
Credentials are write-only: they go in and never come back out.

The key is verified against Bitunix before it is stored, so a typo fails here rather than silently killing the sync loop later. Stored AES-GCM encrypted, with the encryption key in configuration rather than the database.

**Use a read-only key.** TradeLedger never places orders.
Detaches the key and stops automatic syncing for this account. Trades already imported are kept.

request.description:
Supplies what the exchange cannot know. Only the fields you send are changed, so a re-sync never wipes journalling.

Setting a stop loss here also recomputes achieved R, since a synced trade has no stop reported by the exchange. Pass `markReviewed` to clear it from the inbox.

Run **Journal > List strategies** and **List mistakes** first to populate `{{strategyId}}` and `{{mistakeId}}`. Returns the full trade with names resolved.

request.description: Manual trades only. A synced trade cannot be deleted: it would reappear on the next sync sweep, and deleting it would discard the journalling attached to it. Returns 409 if you try.

item.name: Plans
item.description: Pre-trade plans and the position-size calculator.

request.description:
The workbook Calculator sheet as an endpoint, and stateless: sizing a trade should not require committing to it.

Sizes the position so a stop-out loses exactly the risk budget, fees included, then reports order value, margin, take profit at the requested R multiple, and estimated profit and loss net of fees.

`riskFraction` is a fraction, so 0.01 is 1% of balance. Side is inferred from where the stop sits relative to entry.
Pre-trade plans, newest first, optionally filtered by status.

item.name: Analytics
item.description: Performance metrics, equity curve, drawdown and breakdowns. Every endpoint takes the same optional filters.

request.description:
Win rate, gross and net PnL, fees, funding, average win and loss, profit factor, expectancy, planned versus unplanned performance, streaks and average duration.

Profit factor is null rather than infinite when there are no losing trades yet.

Built from balance snapshots, never from summing trades, because spot bags, LP positions and transfers do not appear there.

Returns the curve plus peak equity, max drawdown with the date it happened, and current drawdown.

Slices closed trades by one dimension.

Allowed values: Strategy, Symbol, Side, Timeframe, MarketSession, EntryMentalState, ExitMentalState, DayOfWeek, HourOfDay, Planned.
The discipline metric: does having a plan before entry actually change the outcome?
Performance grouped by how the trader felt at entry.

How often each tagged mistake occurred and what it cost, ordered worst first.

Uses the explicitly attributed cost where one was given, otherwise the net result of the trades the mistake was tagged on.

item.name: Sync
item.description: Bitunix sync status, manual triggers and historical backfill. Every write is idempotent, so re-running is always safe.

request.description: Per account and endpoint: when it last synced, the timestamp of the newest record persisted, and whether the historical backfill has finished.
The last fifty sync attempts with records seen, records written, requests made and any error, so a silently stalled sync is visible.

Forces an incremental reconcile sweep for one account rather than waiting for the scheduled run.

Writes are idempotent, so running this repeatedly is safe and is a no-op when nothing is new.

Walks Bitunix history back to the account `trackedFrom` date. Run once after attaching credentials.

Safe to re-run: every write is an upsert keyed on the exchange position id.

Reads the Bitunix futures wallet and records an equity point.

Bonus is excluded from equity because it is not withdrawable and would inflate the curve.

item.name: Market Data
item.description:
Historical candles behind backtesting: Binance backfill, CSV import, coverage and gaps. Candles are shared rather than per-account, so a symbol only has to be fetched once.

The backfill job requests need a job id. Queue one first; there is no list endpoint to fall back to, so running this folder cold leaves the two status requests without a target.

request.description: What candle history is already stored, per symbol and interval, with the first and last bar and the count. Start here before queueing a backfill.

Missing bars in a range. A rule engine backtest refuses to run over gapped data unless you pass allowGaps, because a missing bar silently skips a signal.

`interval`: FifteenMinutes, ThirtyMinutes, OneHour, TwoHours, FourHours, SixHours, TwelveHours, OneDay, OneWeek. Nothing below fifteen minutes is tradeable; OneMinute exists only for intrabar drill-down.

Pulls candles from Binance through the same egress proxy as Bitunix and stores them. Runs as a background job; poll it with Backfill job status.

Set includeFundingRates to also pull the funding history a futures backtest needs.

One-minute candles are never traded. They exist so the engine can tell whether the stop or the target was hit first inside a bar that touched both. Without them such a bar resolves pessimistically as a stop-out, and the run warns you.
Progress of a queued backfill: candles written, funding rates written, percent complete, and the error if it failed.
Asks the worker to stop. Candles already written are kept; they are valid data regardless of whether the job finished.

For symbols Binance does not carry, or ranges you already exported. Multipart upload: switch the body to form-data, add a `file` field of type File, and `source`, `symbol` and `interval` as text fields.

Duplicate bars are upserted, so re-importing the same file is a no-op.
Removes stored candles so a range can be re-fetched. Finished backtests are untouched: each run keeps its own trades and equity curve.

item.name: Backtests
item.description:
Simulated accounts, strategies and runs. Entirely separate from the live journal: a backtest never creates a Trade, and no journal row is ever produced by a simulation.

Run order matters: create an account and a strategy first, then queue a run. A run needs candle data for its range, so backfill the symbol under Market Data before queueing, or the queue is refused with `candle_data_has_gaps`. That refusal is the point: a missing bar silently skips a signal, and a backtest you cannot trust is worse than none.

request.description:
Simulated balances. Each one is a separate equity curve, so one strategy across hundreds of runs reads as a single account rather than a pile of unrelated results.

Saves the first result to `{{backtestAccountId}}`.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "EMA cross {{runSuffix}}",
  "startingBalance": 10000,
  "description": "Sequential account for the 20/55 EMA cross",
  "currency": "USDT",
  "mode": "Sequential"
}

request.description:
Sequential mode chains runs in date order so each opens at the previous closing balance and sizing compounds; overlapping ranges are then rejected, because compounding the same market twice is fiction.

Independent mode starts every run at the starting balance and is just a folder for comparing variants.

`mode`: Sequential, Independent.
Includes the current balance: the starting balance plus the net result of every succeeded run on a sequential account.
Rename or archive. Switching an account that already has runs to sequential is refused with 409: those runs may overlap in time and chaining them would double-count the same market.
Every run on the account stitched into one curve in date order, with peak-to-trough drawdown measured across the whole chain rather than per run.

Win rate, profit factor, expectancy and streaks over every simulated trade on the account, computed by the same metrics code as GET /api/analytics/summary. That is what makes a backtest comparable to your real trading rather than merely adjacent to it.

Saved rule trees.

Saves the first result to `{{backtestStrategyId}}`.
The indicators a rule may reference, with their outputs and how many warmup bars each needs before it produces a value: Sma, Ema, Rsi, Dmi, Adx.

Parses without saving and reports the warmup bar count the rule needs. Worth knowing: a 55-period EMA on four-hour candles quietly demands 165 bars of prior history before the first signal can fire.

A rejection carries the exact JSON path, for example `$.indicators[0].params.period`.

The rule tree is validated before it is stored, so an unusable strategy never reaches a run.

Exits are not declared here: every position closes on its stop, on a target derived at the run risk-to-reward ratio, or on liquidation. There is no discretionary exit, by design.
One strategy with its full rule tree.
Bumps the version when the rules actually change. Finished runs are untouched: each stores its own copy of the rule JSON and its hash, so an old result stays explainable after the strategy moves on.
Deactivates rather than deletes, so runs that used it stay readable.

Every run, newest first. Filter by accountId, kind or status.

`status`: Queued, Running, Succeeded, Failed, Cancelled.

Saves the first result to `{{backtestRunId}}`.

Queues a simulation and returns 202 straight away; the worker picks it up. Poll it with Get run.

Risk per position is fixed between 1 and 5 percent and read from configuration; risk-to-reward is never below 2. Both are rejected outside those bounds rather than quietly clamped.

The range must not overlap an existing run on a sequential account, and the candle data must have no gaps unless you pass allowGaps.

Status, progress percent, the result summary once it succeeds, and any warnings.

The warning worth reading: if most exits were assumed rather than resolved, the bar held both the stop and the target and no one-minute data could separate them. Backfill one-minute candles for the range and run it again.
